correctness.rationale: Sorting the iid points yields uniform measure on the simplex of n+1 nonnegative spacings with dimension n. A gap exceeding r disconnects all pairs across it, and otherwise adjacent points are joined; only the n−1 internal spacings matter. Because the gap exceedance indicators are exchangeable, conditional on c−1 cuts each cut subset has probability 1/binom(n−1,c−1), and the ordered sizes are its positive spacings between ranks 0 and n. To count the factorial moments, mark the ordered distinct slots of each required size (a_j at size j); distinct sizes cannot share a slot, so there are (c)_A marked injections, each with J(n−S,c−A) completions. This proves the identity also when c=n, A=c, A=0, or the requested marks are infeasible. At c~a√n the ratio is (c)_A(c−1)_A(n−c)_(S−A)/(n−1)_S→a^(2A). All moments of the total of the K selected counts are bounded at any fixed order, by expansion in the mixed factorial moments; this gives tightness and uniform integrability of each fixed mixed moment along subsequences. The product-Poisson law is moment determinate, giving the conditional joint limit. Translating specified simplex coordinates by r gives P(D_i>r all i in a given t-set)=(1−tr)_+^n. For t=1,2 this gives the claimed mean and negative pair-covariance variance bound, and L² convergence of C_n/√n to e^(−x/2). For every bounded continuous test function the deterministic conditional limit is uniform over feasible c in any shrinking rescaled neighborhood of this limit (otherwise select a violating sequence). Choose a shrinking neighborhood whose probability tends to one to decondition. The mean assertion follows separately: for n>j and c≥2 the conditional mean is c(c−1)/(n−1) times (n−c)_(j−1)/(n−2)_(j−1), at most the first factor and asymptotically equal to it in probability; if c=1 the mean is zero for n>j. The bound in the asymptotic proof is used only for n>j, not for j=n,c=1. L² convergence of the rescaled C_n gives L¹ convergence of its square and uniform integrability of the bound. The packaged check was inspected as finite evidence; all claims above follow by the analytic reconstruction.

evidence: Penrose explicitly excludes the hard kernel from the two applicable candidate fixed-order theorems: Theorem 2.2(b) requires supremum o(s^(−1/2)); Theorem 2.3 requires it bounded by 1−ε. The hard kernel equals 1 even for distinct points at short distance.

Han–Makowski Theorem 8.1 is for the total breakpoint count (component count minus one) at all radii, with a quantitative Poisson approximation. Sections VI and X use the same simplex exceedance probabilities, and already yield the concentration of the total count at the half-log window. Their bound does not identify component cardinalities.

Decreusefond–Ferraz's waiting times, length Laplace transform and total-count transform use unconditioned Poisson input. Individual renewal-cluster sizes for an independent exponential-gap construction can be geometric, but this is not a stated fixed-n vector approximation or radius-free conditional census; applying such a method in the fixed-count model would require additional conditioning/coupling and control of overlap and endpoints.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These are real antecedents, but the stronger total-count estimate has the wrong observable, the one-size theorem has the wrong kernel, and the renewal calculations are for a different sampling law.

evidence: The joint cut law in Han–Makowski is fully determined by exceedance probabilities depending only on the number of cut positions; hence the conditional cut exchangeability, and then uniform compositions, follow immediately. The factorial-moment identity is ordinary marked-composition counting, not a separate priority claim for an exact counting technique.

The total-count Poisson theorem cannot substitute for the rare short-separation limit: conditional on the same count c one has many configurations with different size patterns. The singleton Poisson approximation alone likewise does not determine any joint limit for sizes ≥2 or their independence. The crucial extra argument is the square-root fixed-count composition asymptotic across all mixed factorial moments.

The Barbour–Holst abstract and Han–Makowski's citation cover Poisson approximation for large spacings and occupancy; the specific located prior statement concerns the number of breakpoint gaps. No claim that an inaccessible full text lacks a stronger applicable statement is made.

originality.rationale: Best of knowledge, confined to the joint equal-intensity fixed-cardinality spectrum and its quantitative conditional calibration. Han–Makowski already gives the exact simplex cut machinery and stronger estimates of the number of cuts alone, from which the concentration assertion follows. Godehardt–Jaworski provides same-model precedence at least for Poisson approximation of the isolated count, as indicated by the abstract. The conditional uniform composition is an immediate classical symmetry consequence. None of the comparably relevant accessible statements or broader inspected results establishes or directly specializes to the joint census of every fixed finite set of component cardinalities at the isolation window. Historical priority for that distinction remains qualified by the unavailable full text of Godehardt–Jaworski and older discrete allocation work.
residual_risks: The closest 1996 full text could not be inspected: exact priority beyond the identified singleton and total-count overlap is not guaranteed. An inaccessible comparison and unavailable allocation lookup yield no negative evidence.

Older discrete spacings, random-composition, or renewal literature might already express the joint law under an equivalent formulation. The PASS is best-of-knowledge on the inspected evidence, not a historical priority certification.

value.rationale: At the natural isolation scale, knowing either that isolated vertices have a Poisson count or that the total number is of order √n leaves the fragment-size profile undetermined. The equal intensity for every fixed size and their joint independence quantify that profile, while exact conditional moments supply finite-radius calibration. The value is the joint structure rather than rederiving the known isolated-node marginal or proving another connectivity threshold; it does not extend to growing K or nonuniform positions.
